description:
WHEN OTHER at :252-256 - the third and last arm of EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :221-257, reached only once WHEN 0 at :222 and WHEN 13 at :247 have both failed to match. What separates this case from every other read in the set is that nothing about the request is wrong. USERIDI is ADMIN005, which USRSEC genuinely holds at zero-based row 4, and PASSWDI is PASSWORD, which is exactly the password that row stores. The key is right, the record is there, and the read still does not complete. That isolates the unexpected-response arm from the not-found arm as cleanly as the program allows: case05 reaches WHEN 13 by naming a key the file does not hold, so a translation could pass it by mishandling the key, whereas here the key is beyond reproach and only the I/O condition is left to explain the outcome.

The outcome is forced, because it has to be. A keyed EXEC CICS READ against ten well-formed rows can report RESP 0 or RESP 13 and nothing else, so no arrangement of seeded data reaches :252 at all. screenRequest.forcedOutcomes is the harness's declared mechanism for that and is used exactly as declared - one entry, keyed on the read, and nothing else, because the read at :211-219 is the only file operation COSGN00C performs on any path. The outcome named is FileStatus.Outcome.OTHER, which is the vocabulary common/FileStatus.java already defines so that the case and the repository agree on what an outcome is. What SecUserRepository reports for it is SecUserRepository.PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS - the COBOL FILE STATUS '9' followed by a binary x'00' feedback code, which that class documents as landing on precisely this arm - together with no CICS response at all, FileStatus.RESP_NOT_REPORTED rather than a number. No resp is declared beside the outcome, and that is deliberate rather than an omission: :252 is the default of an EVALUATE over raw numeric literals, so it means every response the source did not enumerate and it distinguishes none of them. The real CICS conditions that land here are FileStatus.INVREQ 16, FileStatus.NOTOPEN 19 and FileStatus.LENGERR 22 - an invalid request, a closed file and a length error - and FileStatus.outcomeOfCicsResp maps all three onto Outcome.OTHER because none of them has a status of its own. Naming one of those numbers in the fixture would assert that the arm tells them apart, which :252-256 does not, so the outcome is named and the number is not.

Three outcomes are deliberately not used. ENDFILE belongs to a browse and COSGN00C opens none. DUPKEY is raised on an alternate index and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines no path over USRSEC. DUPREC belongs to a write, and the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE anywhere. Forcing any of the three would describe a response this single keyed read cannot produce, so none of them is fabricated here.

In source order: EIBCALEN is 160, so the cold-start guard at :80-83 is not taken and this is a re-entry with the communication area present; EIBAID is DFHENTER, so :85-95 selects PROCESS-ENTER-KEY rather than the PF3 sign-off at :88-90 or the invalid-key default at :91-94; the RECEIVE MAP at :110-115 delivers both typed fields; EVALUATE TRUE at :117-130 falls through to WHEN OTHER CONTINUE at :128-129 because neither field is SPACES or LOW-VALUES; :132-134 upper-cases USERIDI into WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID and :135-136 upper-cases PASSWDI into WS-USER-PWD, both identity moves here since ADMIN005 and PASSWORD are already upper case, so this case witnesses nothing about the normalisation and does not pretend to - case10 and case16 own that; :138 finds NOT ERR-FLG-ON, the flag still holding the SET ERR-FLG-OFF of :75, and performs READ-USER-SEC-FILE; the read at :211-219 is attempted once on the eight bytes of WS-USER-ID at the KEYLENGTH :216 passes and reports the forced condition; and :221 evaluates WS-RESP-CD, matches neither 0 nor 13, and takes :252.

Stated positively, because it is the crux of the case: the read was attempted, exactly once, on the right key - and it returned no record. USRSEC holds ADMIN005 at row 4 and the seeded block proves it, yet nothing was handed back, so there is no decoded SEC-USER-DATA on this path and no field set belonging to one. That is why row 4 appears in expectedFinalState as a record the run must have left untouched rather than as a record the run read: its six named spans and its eighty-character image are there to show the file is exactly as it was seeded. It is also why :223 is never evaluated at all. The password typed is the correct one and it makes no difference, because a comparison downstream of a read that did not complete does not happen - which is what separates this case from case14, case15 and case17, where the read succeeds and the comparison is the thing that fails.

No role and no transfer target, and this is the strongest form that assertion takes anywhere in the set. :227 moves SEC-USR-TYPE into CDEMO-USER-TYPE and :230 tests 88 CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN, and both sit inside the WHEN 0 arm, so neither executes here: nextProgram is absent, CDEMO-USER-TYPE comes back as the single space it arrived as rather than 'A', and neither of the two XCTL targets - the administrator menu program named by the literal at :232 and the regular-user menu program named by the literal at :237 - is spelt anywhere in this file, which is itself the assertion: a grep for either name over this fixture must come back empty. The choice of key is what makes it the strongest form. ADMIN005 is a genuine administrator in the seeded data, type 'A' at offset 56, so a translation that resolved the role from what the user typed instead of from a record it actually read would name the administrator menu here - and would be caught by this case and by no other in the set. case11 forces the same arm on ADMIN003 and pins the same message; this case pins what the arm does to the role, on a different row, so the two are not one case restated.

The arm body is four statements and each one is pinned. :253 moves 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, so the flag is on - unlike the wrong-password ELSE at :241-246, which is the single rejecting path in this program that sets no flag. :254 moves 'Unable to verify the User ...' into WS-MESSAGE; that literal is twenty-nine characters, counted from the source, and it is the same length as 'Wrong Password. Try again ...' at :242 and 'User not found. Try again ...' at :249 while being different text from both. The three literals are what tell the three arms apart, and confusing them would leave every width assertion satisfied while asserting the wrong path. :255 moves -1 into USERIDL OF COSGN0AI and :256 performs SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN. The message reaches the screen by two moves rather than one: the twenty-nine characters are space-padded into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80), and :149 moves that into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), which truncates on the right because a COBOL MOVE into an alphanumeric receiver truncates on the right. What is pinned is therefore seventy-eight characters, and the two bytes lost are spaces.

The cursor request is USERIDL and it is carried as validation metadata, never as a payload member: the xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items of app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY are length, flag and attribute items, and only the xxxI and xxxO items bear payload. No request is made on PASSWDL. One oddity is preserved rather than tidied. :255 sends the cursor to the user-id field although the failure has nothing to do with what the user typed - the id is valid, the password is valid, and the fault is the file's. The not-found arm at :250 positions the cursor identically, which is presumably where the statement came from. It is the source's behaviour and it stands as written.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - which is 57 - then the named SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once, at seed time, by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation, and is never hand-padded into the rows; the eighty-character expectedFinalState images are what prove the span was emitted as 23 spaces, since a record omitting it would be short by exactly 23. The same job corroborates the width twice over, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) on the cluster it loads; KEYS(8,0) is also why the eight-character key built at :215-216 addresses the whole of SEC-USR-ID and nothing beyond it. There is no usrsec fixture to name - app/data/ASCII holds nine files and none of them is this one - so the rows are stated inline and no tenth fixture is invented. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC, which is the CICS file name at :39 and the FILE definition in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD, and never by a dataset name.

expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion rather than an absence: COSGN00C contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record. expectedDatasets adds the row count and the record width on top of the ten row images, so a dataset that lost or gained a row is caught even where no row-level expectation would notice. expectedReturnCode is 0, and that is worth saying plainly because the instinct runs the other way: an unexpected I/O condition in the batch programs abends, and nine of them do it through CALL 'CEE3ABD'. COSGN00C does not. grep -c RETURN-CODE and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0; the condition is handled as a line on the screen and the transaction returns normally through :98-102. No abend, no raised exception and no non-zero code belongs anywhere in this case - the condition leaves this program as text on line 23 and nothing else.

Determinism, and the two substitutions. SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :147, which opens with MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CURDATE-DATA at :179, so the clock is pinned rather than read: 2022-07-19T23:12:33, traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so that no timezone can shift it. Through app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY is MM '/' DD '/' YY with YY taken from WS-CURDATE-YEAR(3:2) at :188, giving CURDATEO exactly 07/19/22 at its PIC X(8); WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS is HH ':' MM ':' SS, eight characters, moved at :196 into CURTIMEO, which app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:122 declares PIC X(9) - hence 23:12:33 followed by exactly one trailing space. That width is a real trap: the sibling COUSR02 map declares its CURTIMEO PIC X(8) and the two must not be conflated. APPLID and SYSID come from EXEC CICS ASSIGN at :198-200 and :202-204, which has no Java equivalent and which neither application.yml nor application-test.yml binds - both bind the charset keys and neither binds these two - so CICSAWS1 and AWS1 space-padded to PIC X(8) are pinned constants substituting for those calls. All twenty cases use the same pair, and the substitution is stated here rather than hidden. The forced condition is likewise declared in the case data and depends on no timing, no ordering and no property of the environment. The charset is named US-ASCII explicitly, because the authoritative text fixtures are US-ASCII and a platform default is never relied on.

SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN is reached, so the full eleven-item projection of mapset COSGN00 applies, every width taken from the xxxI declarations of app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY and their xxxO redefinitions from :85 onward: TRNNAMEO X(4) carrying CC00, TITLE01O X(40), CURDATEO X(8), PGMNAMEO X(8) carrying COSGN00C, TITLE02O X(40), CURTIMEO X(9), APPLIDO X(8), SYSIDO X(8), USERIDO X(8) handing ADMIN005 back unchanged, PASSWDO X(8) handing PASSWORD back unchanged, and ERRMSGO X(78). The two titles come from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, where line 21 is commented out with an asterisk in column 7 so that line 22 is the active CCDA-TITLE02 - the value is CardDemo centred in forty characters, not the Credit Card Demo Application text the commented line carries. Two nearby literals are neither of these and neither is used on this path: CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU of app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy is PIC X(50) and CCDA-THANK-YOU of COTTL01Y is PIC X(40), different fields at different widths. expectedMessages is empty because app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl contains no DISPLAY anywhere, so there is no emitted line to record - the screen text is an expectation about the send, which is where it is stated.

Two deviations recorded rather than quietly corrected. app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:59 is *COPY DFHATTR. with the asterisk in column 7, which makes it a COBOL comment, so no DFHATTR attribute constant is in effect for this program however many others copy that member - and none is named anywhere here. COSGN00C does not copy CSSETATY either; its only consumer in the repository is COACTUPC, with 39 textual occurrences there and zero here, so no DFHRED plus '*' highlight is applied at run time and no xxxC, xxxP, xxxH or xxxV item is assigned on any path - which is why attributes is empty even on a send that paints an error line. grep returns zero occurrences of CSSETATY, DFHRED and ERRMSGC in this program. The error line is red by static map property, declared once at app/bms/COSGN00.bms:197-200 as ERRMSG DFHMDF ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) COLOR=RED LENGTH=78 POS=(23,1), so the emphasis on this path is that static property together with the USERIDL cursor request and nothing more. Where a run-time attribute value would come from is common/BmsAttributes, which reproduces DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR from IBM CICS documentation because both are IBM-supplied and absent from this checkout - as DFHAID is too, which is also why the attention identifier is named by its common/CicsAid mnemonic DFHENTER and never as a raw byte.

The security posture is unchanged in both directions. The ten seeded rows keep their legacy plaintext SEC-USR-PWD span byte for byte, because :223 compares it in plaintext and digesting the stored value would reject every seeded row and change which requests sign on; nothing is interposed on either side of that comparison - no credential store, no digest, no issued session credential and no security filter chain appears anywhere in this case. One point deserves stating rather than leaving implicit. This arm's message is deliberately different from both the wrong-password text at :242 and the not-found text at :249, so the screen distinguishes a wrong password from an unknown user from a file that would not answer. That is a legacy diagnostic distinction; it is preserved exactly as written, and it is neither endorsed nor unified. A translation that collapsed the three into one message would be changing behaviour, and collapsing them on security grounds would be changing behaviour for a reason this migration has no mandate to act on.

Provenance, stated plainly. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the communication area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy for the two titles, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the header, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes and widths, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for transaction CC00 and the USRSEC file, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases per program, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand, and the substitution is escalated rather than absorbed. No project rules were supplied for this work - review_rules returns the single line stating that no user rules were provided - so none is cited and none is invented, and the enterprise practices the plan names bind instead.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a stubbed SecUserRepository whose read honours the forced outcome - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path, so the arm is reached with nothing between the assertion and the code. Exactly one read is attempted. All conversation state travels in the payload: the sixteen CARDDEMO-COMMAREA fields of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 arrive in the request and leave in the response, one hundred and sixty bytes each way, and only CDEMO-USER-ID differs between them - written unconditionally at :134 and holding ADMIN005 - while CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, CDEMO-USER-TYPE and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT are untouched because :224-228 sits inside the arm this path did not take. No server-side session exists to hold any of it. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the abend gate applies: grep -c 'GO TO' and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0, and neither is faked.
